title: Quantization for Embedded Deep Learning Inference: A Survey and Taxonomy of Camera-Based Perception in Autonomous Driving
content: Quantization is the standard way to run camera perception models for autonomous driving on embedded hardware with far less compute, memory and power than training servers. This paper offers a taxonomy of quantization for embedded camera-based perception in autonomous driving, systematically reviewing 57 peer-reviewed papers published between 2018 and 2026. Selected through a PRISMA 2020 search of Scopus and IEEE Xplore on 22 August 2026, citation searching and a targeted supplementary search on 1 October 2026, the papers are organized by technique and by seven task branches, from two-dimensional detection and segmentation to bird’s-eye-view perception and driver monitoring. Each paper is coded and graded by how directly it measures the effect of reduced precision on the deployed device, which gives practitioners one table to compare methods, hardware and accuracy cost. Results show that eight-bit conversion usually costs little accuracy: in 20 of 32 tests, the accuracy difference between the original and 8-bit versions of the same model was less than two percentage points. Lower numerical precision also provides 1.2–3.9× speedups on the same GPU, FPGA, ARM, and mobile hardware. However, several challenges remain, including significant accuracy losses in some direct conversions, limited same-device comparisons, few power and energy measurements, limited research on bird’s-eye-view perception, and a lack of evaluation on production automotive platforms. The paper closes with a minimum reporting checklist and six research directions for deploying quantized perception in road vehicles.
